added_failures_note: unmeasured: the reviewed manifest names no baseline_suite and no after_suite gate log, so the added-failure count was not taken

findings.text: follow-on: the head gate log's header names rev a1074fb6 (the base) rather than the reviewed commit 173caf43, because the gate ran with the change uncommitted and HEAD still at the base; the manifest's tests line repeats that revision. A reader cannot tie the recorded head arm to the commit from the log alone. The result was independently reproduced at 173caf43 (the equality test passes), so this is a traceability gap, not a false claim.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit 173caf43 against base a1074fb6; one commit, four files, all inside the declared scope (dispatch.py, session_host.py, tests/test_session_host.py, the fragment).
item_verdicts.done_when: the plan's §12 done-when is met: dispatch._session_host_fifo_path(owner) composes from an owner pair, both _session_host_fifo there (dispatch.py:1341) and session_host._fifo_path (session_host.py:221) call it, the format {pid}-{start}.fifo appears once under reckon/ (dispatch.py:1333), and tests/test_session_host.py::test_both_readers_name_one_fifo_for_the_same_owner asserts the two readers agree and fails when one side's format is changed alone.
item_verdicts.goal: the node goal is §12: one Python function names a session host's request FIFO from its owner pair and both readers call it; reckon/crew/dispatch.py:1319 defines _session_host_fifo_path and shares the composition that session_host._fifo_path previously spelled itself.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records the gate over tests/test_session_host.py and tests/test_dispatch_session_host.py at 22 passed EXIT=0, a negative control at gate-negative.log (2 failed EXIT=1), and the single-format count of 1 under reckon/.
item_verdicts.write_paths: read the manifest's declared paths; git show --stat 173caf43 lists reckon/crew/dispatch.py, reckon/crew/session_host.py, tests/test_session_host.py and the evidence fragment, all inside those paths.

justifications.durability: test_both_readers_name_one_fifo_for_the_same_owner pins the invariant and reddens when session_host re-inlines a divergent format; I reproduced both arms in a scratch extraction of 173caf43 (head: 1 passed EXIT=0; the underscore mutation: 1 failed EXIT=1). The bash entry point's own spelling (plugins/crew-host/bin/crew-host:39, $owner_pid-$owner_start.fifo) is unguarded, but the plan carves it out because it cannot import Python, and it composes the same runtime/reckon-session-host/{pid}-{start}.fifo path.
justifications.evidence: the manifest's tests line records the two-file gate at 22 passed EXIT=0 and gate-negative.log holds the 2-failed negative control; I reproduced the equality test at 173caf43 (1 passed) and its declared mutation (1 failed) in a scratch tree, confirming the guard fires.
justifications.fit: _session_host_fifo_path names the mechanism (a FIFO path composed from an owner pair) and its docstring states why the composition lives in dispatch; no plan, sprint or ticket identifier appears in any added name, comment or test id.
justifications.goal_fidelity: dispatch.py:1319 _session_host_fifo_path takes an owner pair and returns root / SESSION_HOST_DIRECTORY / f"{pid}-{start}.fifo"; _session_host_fifo (dispatch.py:1336) and session_host._fifo_path (session_host.py:204) both route through it, so the host removes exactly the file a dispatch writes.
justifications.reuse: the shared function is placed in dispatch, keeping the existing lazy-import direction (session_host imports dispatch deferred), and reuses the existing SESSION_HOST_DIRECTORY and _session_host_runtime_root rather than forking a third spelling; no new module.
justifications.scope_discipline: git show --stat 173caf43 lists only the four declared paths; the path's format and location are unchanged and the bash entry point still names the same file.
